senses.sense_definition: A prison design where all cells are visible from a central point, making inmates feel constantly watched.

examples.text: The architect designed the prison as a <w>panopticon</w> to ensure guards could monitor every cell from the center.
Living in the small apartment felt like being in a <w>panopticon</w> because the neighbors could see into every room.

senses.sense_definition: A system or environment where individuals are subject to constant, pervasive surveillance.

examples.text: Many critics argue that modern digital tracking has turned the internet into a global <w>panopticon</w>.
The government created a digital <w>panopticon</w> to monitor the activities of all its citizens.

senses.sense_definition: An early type of projector used in the 18th and 19th centuries.

examples.text: The museum displayed an antique <w>panopticon</w> used for projecting images during the nineteenth century.
Historians studied the old <w>panopticon</w> to understand early methods of visual entertainment.

senses.sense_definition: A room or space dedicated to displaying new or unusual items.

examples.text: The gallery opened a new <w>panopticon</w> to showcase the latest inventions from local artists.
Visitors gathered in the <w>panopticon</w> to see the collection of rare artifacts.
